items.caption:
Why can't I sleep in a new place? It's called the first-night effect.
In a 35-person study, part of the left brain slept lighter on night one and woke people faster to odd sounds. By night two, the difference was gone.

items.caption:
Do your dreams replay your day?
Rarely in full: about 2 in 3 dreams borrowed pieces of recent life, but full replays were 1-2%. Another study found a second echo 5 to 7 days later, the dream-lag effect.
What did last night's dream borrow from your week?

items.caption:
Dreaming of falling?
In a survey of 1,181 students, about 74% had dreamed of falling at least once. Separately, a falling feeling can come with the hypnic jerk, the jolt 60 to 70% of people report as they drift off.
Falling, chased, or losing teeth: which one comes back for you?
